quote: Welches ist die allgemeine Bedingung, damit in einem Integritätsbereich die gewöhnlichen Teilbarkeitsgesetze gelten oder wenigstens [-…-] bei Ein- führung idealer Zahlen.
english: What is the general condition for the ordinary laws of divisibility to hold in an integral domain, or at least to hold once ideal numbers are introduced?
topic: The page covers systems (number domains) closed under operations, with examples from ring and field theory, questions on when divisibility laws hold in integral domains, and a plan for teaching function theory by combining Weierstrass with Riemann–Cauchy.

triage.modern_statement: Find the exact conditions on an integral domain R for (a) the usual laws of divisibility to hold, meaning R is a unique factorization domain (UFD): every nonzero nonunit factors into irreducibles, and every irreducible is prime. Also find the conditions for (b) a weaker version: divisibility works once 'ideal numbers' are added, as in Kummer and Dedekind. In modern terms, (b) asks when every nonzero ideal factors uniquely into prime ideals (a Dedekind domain), or more generally when divisors factor uniquely (a Krull domain / divisor theory).
triage.answered_by: The ideal-number part was answered by Emmy Noether in 'Abstrakter Aufbau der Idealtheorie in algebraischen Zahl- und Funktionenkörpern' (Math. Annalen, 1926/27). She showed that ideals factor uniquely into prime ideals exactly when the domain is Noetherian, integrally closed in its field of fractions, and every nonzero prime ideal is maximal (Krull dimension at most 1). That is the axiomatic description of Dedekind domains. Wolfgang Krull's theory of Krull domains (late 1920s to 1930s) extended this to higher dimensions: a domain is a UFD exactly when it is a Krull domain with trivial divisor class group. This is now standard textbook commutative algebra.

evidence.claim: Noether's 1921 'Idealtheorie in Ringbereichen' and 1926 'Abstrakter Aufbau der Idealtheorie' carried Dedekind's theory of algebraic integers over to arbitrary integral domains and general rings.

A Dedekind ring is a Noetherian integral domain that is integrally closed and in which every nonzero prime ideal is maximal. The source cites Noether's 'Abstrakter Aufbau der Idealtheorie' as a reference.

For an integral domain that is not a field, being a Dedekind domain (unique factorization of ideals into prime ideals) is equivalent to being integrally closed, Noetherian and of Krull dimension one. Every PID is a Dedekind domain.
To study UFDs in dimension greater than one, the class of Dedekind domains is widened to Krull domains. A UFD is exactly a Krull domain in which every divisorial ideal is principal.
A UFD is a Krull domain with trivial divisor class group. Current research still refines this in specific settings, such as the Samuel–Grothendieck theorem.

triage.why: Hilbert's question asks when an integral domain has unique factorization, either of elements or of ideals. Both versions were settled in the 1920s–30s: Noether's 1926 work gave the axioms for unique factorization of ideals (Dedekind domains), and Krull's theory showed that a UFD is a Krull domain with trivial class group. The question is not one of Hilbert's 23 published problems. Factorization theory in general is still studied, for example non-unique factorization and class groups, but the question as Hilbert stated it is a standard solved result. The sources found do not tie Noether's work directly to this diary note, so any historical influence is not established.
